 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioners in O.P.(MV) No.162/2017 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
North Paravur (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 14/01/2019.

Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
North Paravur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The sole respondent herein is the 3rd respondent in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.
2. The claim petitioners are the wife and children of deceased Joseph.

According to the claim petitioners, on 10/01/2017 at about 10:30 a.m., while the deceased Joseph was standing by the side of Aluva-Alangad road at the place by name Parambayam, scooter bearing registration no.KL-45-E-5107 2025:KER:40780 ridden by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, whereby he sustained grievous injuries, to which he succumbed on 22/01/2017.
3. The first respondent/owner remained ex parte.
4. The second respondent/rider filed written statement disputing the negligence of the deceased.

sentences.text: Third respondent/insurer filed written statement contending that the accident was caused solely due to the negligence of the deceased.
Since there was no negligence on the part of the second respondent, the claim petitioners are not entitled to get compensation.
The age, occupation and monthly income of the deceased were disputed.
The compensation claimed under various heads was contended to be exorbitant.
6. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A8 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.

7. The Tribunal on consideration of the 2025:KER:40780 documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent-rider of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 8,70,898/- together with interest @
7.5% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioners have come up in appeal.
8.
The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
9. Heard both sides 10.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners that the deceased was a married man and that the claim petitioners are his widow and children.

That being the position, one half that has been deducted by the Tribunal from his income towards the personal expenses of the deceased while computing loss of future prospects is not correct in the light of the dictum in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corp., (2009)6 SCC 2025:KER:40780 121.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In support of this argument, reference is made to the judgment of the Apex Court in Babita Singh v. New India Assurance Company Ltd., 2024 ACJ 223.

entities.text: Babita Singh v. New India Assurance Company Ltd., 2024 ACJ 223
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This argument is not contested by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer.
Hence, the deduction towards personal expenses from the income of the deceased will be only 1/3rd.
To the said effect, the Award shall stand modified.
Loss of consortium
Admittedly, the second and third claim petitioners are the children of the deceased.

In the light of the dictum in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram, (2018) 18 SCC 130: 2018 KHC 6697, they are entitled to compensation towards loss of parental consortium at the rate of 40,000/- each.
